purpose: The cross-repo generalization of architecture/portfolio_dependency_law.json for the MULTI-REPO org. Each product surface is a SEPARATE GitHub repo under one org account. A surface becomes AWARE of another ONLY through that surface's published interface manifest (interface.json) — never by importing its source. This file is the single machine-readable registry of surfaces, what each EXPOSES, and which others it MAY consume. Enforced by tools/check_cross_repo_dependency_law.py in each repo's CI, so the boundary is a proof, not prose.
law: Dependency direction is preserved across repos: Baltor -> Teleon -> OpenHubForAI, never the reverse. Every product surface may consume SharedBackendComponents (the substrate) and the OpenHubForAI open spec. A surface consumes another ONLY via its published interface.json (a versioned contract), never its internals. dev-rules-context is inherited by every repo (standards + gates) and depends on nothing.

_needs_owner_confirmation.openhubforai_placement: Owner's repo list (AiDoneRight, Teleon, Baltor, AIDevObserver, SharedBackendComponents, dev-rules, 'etc') did not name OpenHubForAI explicitly. Kept as its own neutral surface here (it stewards the open spec); confirm whether it is its own repo or folded into SharedBackendComponents.
_needs_owner_confirmation.consumption_mechanism: How a consumed interface is delivered across repos (git submodule of a published-interfaces repo, a versioned package, or generated client stubs) is an owner infra choice — the CONTRACT (interface.json) is the same regardless.

consumption_rule: surface A may reference surface B's capabilities ONLY through B's interface.json (name + version + exposes). Importing B's source from A is a forbidden cross-repo edge, caught by the checker.

dev-rules-context.role: the standards + gates + shared-context TEMPLATE repo (this template-repo). Inherited by every other repo; holds the naming law, multi-path methodology, verification laws, the surface registry, and the portable checkers.

shared-backend-components.role: the SUBSTRATE every product consumes — the primitive/component registry + factory + catalog, codegraph, naming planes, eval, storage tiers, pipelines, credential plane. Reusable infrastructure, product-neutral.

openhubforai.role: the OPEN ecosystem + the open CapabilityTask spec (CTS). The neutral home of the standard; stays product-neutral.

teleon.role: the purpose-driven, eval-gated, self-adaptive compute RUNTIME SaaS. Owns PurposeTask/CapabilityTask, runtime selection, evidence ledger, promotion/policy gates, adapters, the assurance dashboard. Reference implementation of the open spec.

baltor.role: the applied, customer-facing CONTEXT product, powered by Teleon (a TENANT). Governance / provenance / signed facts / CDC is the moat.

aidevobserver.role: the AI-USAGE layer — session/AI-usage coaching (not code review); MCP + CLI + extension + app + local service.

aidoneright.role: the PARENT BRAND / portfolio umbrella (aidoneright.dev). References every surface's PUBLIC interface for the portfolio site; owns no product logic.
aidoneright._note: aidoneright consumes only PUBLISHED interfaces (for display/routing), never product internals.

api-endpoint-wrappers.role: DEV TOOL — reusable adapters that wrap third-party / local / cloud API endpoints behind stable PORTS (agnostic-adapter pattern), so every product calls a capability, never a hardcoded host. Cost-ordered, deterministic-first.

scraping.role: DEV TOOL — reusable scraping / browser-automation / stealth-fetch toolkit (the descent ladder: API -> browser -> stealth -> vision). Feeds intake/discovery. Consented + governed only.

context-injection.role: DEV TOOL — reusable context assembly / packing / memory / prompt-composition tooling (context packs, headroom compression, retrieval-into-prompt). The 'context is everything' plumbing every agent surface uses.

business-context.role: CONTEXT repo — business notes, decisions (with warrants), activity log, analytics, MCP server configs, meeting/strategy notes. 'Context in a repo': the durable business memory every surface can reference, separate from product code.
business-context._note: context-only, no product code; decisions carry warrants (change-verification law); read by humans + agents for grounding, never imported as code.

edge-graph-generator.role: META DEV TOOL — reads the surface-registry + every repo's published interface.json and GENERATES the repo-to-repo edge context + dependency graph: a compact per-repo edge digest (a session on repo X sees X + its neighbors' EDGES, never their internals) plus the global graph. Keeps cross-repo awareness in sync without full-context reads.
edge-graph-generator._note: reads interface manifests (contracts) only, never repo source; its output is what makes 'edge-aware, not everything-aware' real.

pitch-decks.role: CONTEXT repo — investor pitch decks, investment narrative, one-pagers, traction/metrics evidence. The outward-facing fundraising STORY every investor conversation draws from, separate from product code and internal business memory.
pitch-decks._note: context-only, no product code; public/synthetic metrics only (no confidential data); cites the brand + product story via aidoneright's public face.

yc-applications.role: CONTEXT repo — Y Combinator (and other accelerator) application drafts, answers, founder/video scripts, readiness scoring, demo storyboard. The application artifacts, separate from product code.
yc-applications._note: context-only; yc-readiness is COMPUTED by scripts/yc_readiness.py (not asserted); public/synthetic only.

fundraising.role: CONTEXT repo — go-to-market + fundraising strategy, investor outreach, round planning, market sizing. The money/market PLAN, separate from the deck itself and from product code.
fundraising._note: context-only; strategy carries warrants (change-verification law); public/synthetic only.

forbidden_edges.why: Teleon is reusable infrastructure, never Baltor-specific
the open spec stays neutral; Teleon consumes OHH, not the reverse
the open ecosystem must not require the applied product
the substrate is product-neutral; products consume it, not the reverse
substrate must not depend on a product
the rules/standards repo depends on nothing — it is inherited, not a consumer

_decomposition_note: A SURFACE is a product family; a PROJECT is a deployable repo (backend/frontend/microservice/client). Frontends consume their backend via its published API; cross-surface deps go backend-to-backend. code_path = where the code lives in the monolith TODAY, to be git-moved into the project repo at split time (the risky migration step, not yet performed).
_capability_catalog_note: Single source for the one-line meaning of every exposed capability id. interface_manifests.py fills each interface.json exposes[].summary from here (via --sync), so the machine contract documents WHAT each capability does, not just its id. Keep one entry per id used in any surface's exposes.

capability_catalog.standards/*: The eight inherited org laws (multi-path, globally-unique naming, candidate/truth boundary, change-verification, verify-the-verifier, no-magic-values, lossless-distillation, archival).
capability_catalog.contracts/surface-registry.json: The single source of truth for every surface: its exposes, allowed may_depend_on edges, and forbidden edges.
capability_catalog.tools/check_*.py: Portable enforcement gates every repo runs (cross-repo dependency law, interface-manifest consistency).
capability_catalog._shared/*: Common truth every repo references: the glossary, architecture map, single-source config constants, and the id-minting authority.
capability_catalog.registry: The federated component/primitive registry behind one Registry<T> port (uniform list/lookup/search/explain).
capability_catalog.primitives: The seven canonical primitives (Input, Knowledge Corpus, If Statement, Action, Loop, Stop/End, Output) and their composition edges.
capability_catalog.codegraph: The tree-sitter AST symbol/edge graph over the codebase (callers, callees, impact, change-audit).
capability_catalog.eval-harness: The two-axis lift+durability gap harness that admits a component only if it lifts over the bare model AND the lift is structural.
capability_catalog.storage-tiers: The tiered record store: config JSON, operational Postgres+pgvector, and history warehouse.
capability_catalog.credential-plane: The single-source credential registry — env-var names only, deny-by-default reachability.
capability_catalog.capabilitytask-spec: The open CapabilityTask Spec (CTS): the neutral, portable definition of an executable capability.
capability_catalog.eval-harnesses: Open evaluation harnesses for scoring capability lift in the ecosystem.
capability_catalog.conformance-tests: Conformance suites that prove an implementation meets the CTS.
capability_catalog.skills: The open library of composable skills/Actions.
capability_catalog./api/teleon: The runtime SaaS API: PurposeTask submission, runtime selection, and receipts.
capability_catalog.PurposeTask: The core runtime object (formal synonym CapabilityTask): a purpose + guardrails compiled to an optimized, verified execution graph.
capability_catalog.runtime-selector: Cost-ordered, deterministic-first selection of the execution path, bounded by the org guardrail policy.
capability_catalog.evidence-ledger: The append-only receipt store recording every run's cost, accuracy, and decisions.
capability_catalog.promotion-gate: The proof-gated boundary that promotes a candidate to served truth — never self-promoted.
capability_catalog.assurance-portal: The customer-facing Capability Assurance Portal (runtime health, receipts, policy).

capability_catalog.governance: Provenance, signed facts, and CDC/revocation — the external moat; serves_truth=true only after review.
capability_catalog.customer-workflows: Vertical, customer-facing capability workflows (e.g. sanctions screening, provider directory).
capability_catalog.receipts: Per-answer provenance receipts: source handles, lineage, and verification status.
capability_catalog./api/observer: The AI-usage layer API: session/AI-usage coaching (not code review).
capability_catalog.session-review: Consented-session review that mines AI-coding sessions into tools, research-queue items, and registry candidates.
capability_catalog.mcp-server: The Claude Code MCP connection that surfaces live reuse hints.
capability_catalog.cli: The command-line client for session review and primitive refresh.
capability_catalog.portfolio-site: The parent brand site (aidoneright.dev) referencing every surface's public face.
capability_catalog.brand: The parent brand system ('AI, done right.') and design family.
capability_catalog.port-adapters: Reusable adapters that wrap third-party/local/cloud API endpoints behind a stable port.
